$comment: Exceptions to the container image CVE gate (scripts/supply-chain/container-scan.mjs).
Empty by design. Every entry MUST carry a reason, an approver and an expiry date;
the gate fails on an entry missing any of them, fails on an entry whose `expires` is
not a valid ISO date, and fails again once that date passes — so an exception cannot
quietly become permanent. It is the same shape and the same rules as
scripts/supply-chain/osv-allowlist.json, deliberately: two allowlists that behave
differently is how somebody learns the wrong rule.
An entry here suppresses a finding the gate would otherwise BLOCK on. It does not
suppress the finding from the report: an allowed CVE is still printed, still counted
and still named with its expiry, because an exception nobody can see is an exception
This is NOT where unfixable base-image CVEs go. The gate already declines to block on
a finding with no available fix (see `--include-unfixed` in container-scan.mjs) and
reports them in their own section, because the only remediation for one is changing
base image and a list of thirty entries nobody reads is worse than a number somebody
does. Use this for a finding that IS fixable and that you are deliberately shipping
anyway, for a stated reason, until a stated date.
Schema: { id, package?, image?, reason, expires (ISO date), approvedBy }
